record.paper_title: Open problems in theory of metric linear spaces
record.context_brief: Spaces without unbounded norms and copies of s
record.original_question: If an F-space has no unbounded norm, must it contain a copy of the sequence space s of all scalar sequences?

evidence.quote: It is not known does each space without unbounded norm contains the space s .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\|\cdot\|)$ be an F-space, i.e., a topological vector space over the scalar field $\mathbb{K}\in\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}\}$ whose topology is induced by a complete translation-invariant metric, with associated F-norm $\|\cdot\|:X\to[0,\infty)$ satisfying $\|x\|=0\iff x=0$, $\|\lambda x\|\le\|x\|$ for $|\lambda|\le 1$, and $\lim_{\lambda\to 0}\|\lambda x\|=0$ for every $x\in X$. A continuous F-norm $p$ on $X$ (i.e., a continuous function with the same properties as above) is called unbounded if $\sup_{x\in X}p(x)=\infty$. Say that $X$ has no unbounded norm if every continuous F-norm on $X$ is bounded.

Let $s$ denote the F-space of all scalar sequences $(x_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ equipped with the topology of coordinatewise convergence, which is metrizable by the complete F-norm
$$\|(x_n)\|_s=\sum_{n=1}^\infty 2^{-n}\frac{|x_n|}{1+|x_n|}.$$

Question: Must every F-space $X$ with no unbounded norm contain a closed linear subspace topologically isomorphic to $s$?
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution was found in the search. The problem is stated as an unsolved question in the functional-analytic literature on metric linear spaces, and standard references on F-spaces and sequence spaces do not record a proof or counterexample.

status_evidence.title: F-space - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: An F-space is a topological vector space whose topology is induced by a complete translation-invariant metric.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the standard definition of F-space used in the problem; no resolution of the question is indicated.

status_evidence.title: Sequence space - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The space s of all scalar sequences with the topology of coordinatewise convergence is a Fréchet space.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the standard meaning of the space s but does not address the embedding question.
